messages:
sean: quick note — tried an nsight capture to reproduce the kv-batching perf regression. used trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt and a short sample window. results are... messy.
anya: ok what flags did you run? can you paste the exact CLI?
sean: pasted below — short run to keep file small:
```
nsys profile --output=kvbatch-quick --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \n  --sample=cpu --sample-cpu-interval=500 \n  --force-overwrite --duration=35s \n  --capture-range=nvtx:1..100
```
sean: key observations: kernel timeline shows a burst of tiny kernels (~200-500us) before the large attention kernels; nvtx markers for request boundaries line up intermittently (osrt sampling misses some markers).
devon: that sounds like sampling bias — short kernels often get under-sampled so nvtx brackets look off. did you try a bracketed capture (start/stop around the hot request)?
sean: I did a bracketed run too, but the bracket was still too coarse. when I narrowed to a 6s capture around the hotspot the nvtx alignment improved, but then we lost context for batch formation warmup.
anya: curious — did you see a kernel switch? like fused_attention -> attention_opt_v2 around batch size 8?
sean: yes. timeline shows selection flip at ~12s into the capture when the batch aggregator moved from size 6 -> 9. single-kernel latencies:
```
fused_attention: 1.20 ms (median)
attention_opt_v2: 0.86 ms (median)
kv_prefetch_kernel: 0.18 ms (median)
```
sean: but the overall request latency regressed because we started seeing extra kv-evict kernels interleaved during the larger batches. those eviction kernels are triggered when the kvcache size hits a threshold at scale-up.
maria: do you have the full nvtx timeline snippet? can we see whether the evict kernels are inside the same nvtx bracket as the attention kernels?
sean: fragments: evict kernels often land between the request NVTX start and the attention NVTX marker — so they aren't being accounted for in our per-request token time. that's likely why our SLO telemetry underreports.
anya: hunch: osrt sampling + short capture window -> some OS thread timelines are collapsed and nsight's thread-based grouping splits the nvtx spans. try adding `--sample=none` for one run (full trace, longer duration) to get deterministic NVTX capture, then do a short sampled run to find hotspots.
devon: also try `--capture-range=cuda:kernel` style to force continuous GPU capture for the critical period. that avoids the heuristic OSRT slicing.
sean: good tips. I'll run two followups: (A) full capture 120s with `--sample=none` and explicit `--capture-range=nvtx:200..450` around the failing scenario, (B) a short 20s high-res capture with `--sample=cpu --sample-cpu-interval=200`.
infra-bot: FYI, long full captures will generate ~1.2GB/min on these nodes. schedule off hours or use the perf-lab queue. :warning:
maria: thanks — when you have the full trace, can you extract the kernel selection table + per-kernel memory throughput? that will help confirm whether attention_opt_v2 is using a different shared memory tiling that causes evictions.
sean: will do. action items: run A/B captures, upload to perf bucket, add a short comment on the timeline where kvcache crosses threshold. I'll ping here when done.
anya: if you want, I can add a small wrapper script to produce consistent capture flags (bracket + sample combo) so we don't reintroduce this noise.
sean: please — wrapper would help. thanks all. :thumbsup:
